name: @sos-2/task-graph
description: SOS 2.0 Durable Task Graph (Work Order P6): the mission-linked, authority-pinned durable work graph of the Spirit Orchestrator. Every TaskNode carries a MISSION REFERENCE and an AUTHORITY REFERENCE (pinned by tests — no task exists outside mission + authority), an owned-path scope (assignment onto DISJOINT scopes only — a collision is a typed assignment denial, never silent overlap), validated acyclic dependencies, a typed six-state machine (PENDING/RUNNING/PAUSED/CANCELLED/COMPLETED/FAILED — typed transitions only, COMPLETED is VERIFICATION-GATED: the final verification record gates the transition and a worker completion report never certifies), the checkpoint chain, retries/recovery state (a failed task is marked RETRYABLE, never silently done), unresolved uncertainty, the cost envelope and the final verification record ref. The full section 6 task-durability field list of spec/productization-execution-architecture.md is representable field-for-field (pinned by tests). Crash safety: worker crashes, provider outages and body loss produce TYPED task failures that leave the graph structurally valid — invariant scans + property tests pin no orphaned references, no partial writes and no lost tasks. Persistence is append-only through the P2 live-store task records VERBATIM: the node snapshot serializes into the record's plan field and every section 6 field maps natively onto the P2 TaskRecord shape; the store never redefines the graph's shapes. Identity discipline: task ids are caller-supplied RUNTIME identifiers (no local identity minting; spine-shaped ids are rejected loudly); mission and authority references are spine artifact ids validated by the spine's own guards. Determinism: no Date.now/Math.random/fetch/process.env in this package's src — the clock and stores are injected.
